children: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. (BABA, Financials) has been developing Qwen as a significant AI platform for years. Now Washington wants to know how some of that progress was made.
U.S. intelligence and cybersecurity officials have accused Chinese developers, including Alibaba, DeepSeek and Moonshot AI, of harvesting massive amounts of data from American frontier models.
The activity dates to at least 2024 and included billions of tokens across millions of requests, officials claimed. The controversy centers on a process called distillation.
That's common protocol in AI. Stronger models' outputs are used by developers to help train smaller or cheaper systems. The issue, according to U.S. authorities, is scale and access.
They said Chinese developers exploited American models in ways that may have broken regulations intended to protect private technology. China has denied the allegations.
The technical argument itself is not the immediate issue for Alibaba investors. What matters is what Washington does next.
Tighter access restrictions, new compliance requirements and other technology limits might make it harder for Chinese AI startups to compete abroad.
Next, investors should monitor to see if this warning develops into actual policy, particularly as Alibaba is trying to expand Qwen outside of China.

title: Alibaba Just Got Pulled Into a Bigger U.S.-China AI Fight
